Header:

Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Emily Carter (Northstar Head of Security), Dr. Aaron Miles (CTO), Samir Patel (Cloud Engineer), Leah Wong (Compliance)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO options, audit log retention, and options for customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK/HSM). Agreed next steps to share reports and schedule a technical deep dive.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, Trust Center, controls mapping, RBAC, SAML/SSO, audit logs, data residency, encryption/KMS, private deployment vs hosted, pen test reports.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we've got -- we scheduled about 55 minutes, we'll run through the posture items then leave time for questions. Priya and Marco from my team are here to handle the deep technical bits.
[00:18] Emily Carter: Great thanks Jordan, I'm Emily, I run security at Northstar. Quick context — we're doing a vendor risk review for Q4, need assurance for PHI processing and some residency constraints for our EU patients. We'll need SOC 2 and ISO artefacts plus trust center access.
[00:35] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. To set expectations, Redwood keeps a trust center with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 materials; we'll share the relevant summary pack after this call. We support hosted, dedicated and private deployments — you can pick a VPC/private control plane if you need stricter data residency.
[00:52] Dr. Aaron Miles: Quick clarifying q — for PHI encryption at rest do you support customer-managed keys/HSM? We need to ensure we can rotate keys and have control.
[01:05] Marco Alvarez: Yep, good question. We offer BYOK — bring your own key — via KMS integrations. For cloud deployments we integrate with major KMS providers and you can host keys in your HSM. There's a flow for key rotation and we can provide sample IAM policies.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Is that available for hosted or only for private/dedicated? Our preference is hosted due to cost but we have strict key control needs.
[01:30] Priya Nair: Right now customer-managed keys are supported for Redwood Private and for Dedicated in some configurations; for fully hosted accounts we have envelope encryption and we can support CMK for enterprise plans — Marco will follow up with specific architecture docs. Sometimes the hosted offering is misheard as 'Redwood Dedicate' in notes — apologies for any confusion.
[01:51] Emily Carter: Ok. Also, audit logs — what event retention do you provide and can we ship logs to our SIEM? We need 1 year retention for auth events and 3 years for admin changes ideally.
[02:06] Marco Alvarez: We keep detailed audit logs, can forward via syslog/secure transfer or cloud-native subscriptions. Retention defaults depend on plan; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and exporters. We'll share the matrix in the trust center link. Quick caveat: some auto-generated logs may have noisy fields and display user ids differently — transcription note: sometimes usernames appear as Speaker 1 or system ids.
[02:30] Leah Wong: For SOC 2 scope, which services does Redwood cover? We need to map controls to your boundaries.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: Our SOC 2 covers the Redwood-hosted API and the control plane components for the hosted product. For Dedicated and Private, the SOC 2 report covers Redwood's managed services — for customer-managed infra (on-prem), the customer inherits some controls; we'll provide a controls mapping doc so you can see which controls are shared vs ours.
[02:55] Emily Carter: Perfect. Can you also provide pen test reports or at least a summary?
[03:02] Priya Nair: We have third-party penetration test summaries and vulnerability management artifacts; full reports are available under NDA. We'll include redacted summaries in the shared pack.
[03:12] Dr. Aaron Miles: Data residency — we have EU datasets that must not leave region. What's your region segmentation?
[03:20] Marco Alvarez: Redwood has region-aware routing and dedicated regions; with Private you can deploy in a customer VPC in EU-West and ensure data residency. For hosted, we offer region pinning for enterprise accounts, but please note some ancillary services may be in a central control plane — we'll call that out in the controls mapping.
[03:40] Samir Patel: A common compliance snag is service-to-service logs and telemetry sent to a central observability stack. Are those encrypted and can we limit what telemetry leaves the region?
[03:51] Priya Nair: Observability telemetry is encrypted in transit and at rest; for Private we can keep the observability stack in-region. For hosted, telemetry for platform metrics may be aggregated across regions but we can provide a data flow diagram and map out what leaves region.
[04:10] Emily Carter: About SSO — we use SAML with Okta; we need SCIM user provisioning and role mapping to manage admin vs viewer privileges. How granular is your RBAC?
[04:21] Jordan Lee: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin, operator, viewer and custom roles; audit logs capture role changes. We'll share a step-by-step for mapping Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[04:37] Leah Wong: Does SSO also cover service accounts and API keys? We need separate auditability for API keys and ability to restrict by route/model.
[04:46] Marco Alvarez: API keys are auditable; you can segment keys per route and per project. We also recommend using short-lived session tokens and rotating keys regularly. For stricter setups, Private allows service accounts backed by KMS.
[05:01] Samir Patel: Are there known issues with KV cache logs or token leakage in cache traces? We've seen traces in other vendors.
[05:10] Priya Nair: Good callout — KV cache debug logs should not contain sensitive prompt content; we have redaction and masking in place. We'll share the cache handling doc. Note: sometimes internal docs call it 'K V cache' in transcripts.
[05:28] Emily Carter: On ISO 27001 — do you have scope and certificate? We need the certificate and which annex controls are implemented.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, ISO 27001 is in scope for the main control plane and key services; certificate available in Trust Center. The controls mapping will show which Annex A controls we map to Redwood processes.
[05:48] Dr. Aaron Miles: For our legal team, we also need evidence of data deletion for offboarding — do you provide verified deletion proofs or logs?
[05:58] Marco Alvarez: We provide documented offboarding processes and deletion logs; for some storage layers we can provide deletion confirmations and timestamps. For high-assurance needs we can discuss additional verification workflows.
[06:12] Emily Carter: Can we get a demo of the Trust Center UI? I want to see how artifacts are surfaced.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Yep we can share a read-only Trust Center link. We'll send an access invite post-call.
[06:24] Emily Carter: Great. Also curious about the security of model weights and model provenance — do you have attestations for model artifacts?
[06:33] Priya Nair: We maintain model provenance records and signed checksums; for curated models we can surface vetting notes. Model weights for hosted models are stored with access controls; for Private deployments the customer controls model storage.
[06:45] Samir Patel: If we do a Dedicated deployment, what's the upgrade / patch process? We need maintenance windows and SLA for security patches.
[06:55] Marco Alvarez: For Dedicated we provide scheduled patch windows with advance notice, emergency patching for critical CVEs with a playbook, and change logs. We'll include the maintenance SLA in the attachments.
[07:08] Emily Carter: A red flag for us is long-tail log retention costs; how flexible is the exporter to our S3 bucket or SIEM?
[07:17] Marco Alvarez: You can export logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies, or stream to Splunk/Datadog. The retention policy is configurable on Dedicated/Private; hosted has some limits but we can set up cross-account delivery for enterprise.
[07:32] Dr. Aaron Miles: On encryption in transit — TLS versions, mutual TLS for internal services?
[07:36] Priya Nair: We enforce TLS 1.2+ for external traffic and TLS 1.3 where supported. Mutual TLS is available for certain private peering setups.
[07:48] Emily Carter: OK -- from a controls point of view can you provide the mapping to our standard SOC matrix (CCM)?
[07:54] Jordan Lee: We'll provide a controls mapping spreadsheet we usually share with customers; it maps SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO Annex controls, and Redwood responsibilities vs customer responsibilities.
[08:05] Emily Carter: For encryption keys — does Redwood ever have access to plaintext with BYOK?
[08:11] Marco Alvarez: With proper BYOK/HSM configuration the operator cannot decrypt without key material; Redwood does not have access to plaintext if the key is customer-kept. We'll provide the architecture diagram to show the envelope encryption flow.
[08:24] Samir Patel: Good. For pen tests, are there recurring scans and do you run internal code reviews for dependency vulns?
[08:33] Priya Nair: Yes we run regular pentests annually and vulnerability scanning with SCA for dependencies; remediation SLAs are in our policy documents.
[08:43] Emily Carter: Any noteworthy open issues in the last 12 months? We need a risk summary.
[08:49] Jordan Lee: We maintain a security posture report with historical findings; most items were low/medium and remediated within SLA. We'll share the high-level summary; full details under NDA.
[09:02] Dr. Aaron Miles: What about privacy — do you have DPA and standard contractual clauses for EU data?
[09:09] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have a DPA and SCCs available. For EU customers we offer data processing addendums and region controls.
[09:18] Leah Wong: A practical step — we'll want to kick off mapping our internal control requirements to Redwood's controls and flag any gaps; who should own that?
[09:27] Emily Carter: I'll own the mapping on our side; Jordan if you can provide the template and trust center artifacts that should be enough to start.
[09:34] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Back to the technical nuance — audit log granularity: we log API calls, model inference metadata (not raw prompt contents unless configured), admin actions, role changes and auth events.
[09:49] Samir Patel: About raw prompt content — for our workflows we sometimes need to persist prompts for debugging. Can we opt in and get them encrypted with our keys?
[09:58] Marco Alvarez: You can opt in for persistence, and with Private/Dedicated and BYOK you can encrypt those persisted prompts under your keys. For hosted we recommend redaction and short TTLs.
[10:12] Emily Carter: Great. Any blockers you foresee for SOC/ISO evidence?
[10:18] Priya Nair: Mostly NDA for full reports and some architecture diagrams; otherwise we provide summaries and the mapping. If you need keys in HSM we can discuss deployment timelines.
[10:28] Dr. Aaron Miles: Can you provide tech contact for a follow-up deep dive on the KMS integration?
[10:33] Jordan Lee: Marco will be the point on KMS and Priya on RBAC/audit logs. We'll coordinate a session with Samir and your infra folks.
[10:41] Emily Carter: Ok let's recap next steps — send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, Trust Center link, controls mapping, KMS design doc, schedule deep dive.
[10:52] Jordan Lee: Yep, we'll do that. Anything else?
[10:56] Leah Wong: Nothing from me. Thanks everyone.
[11:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with links and action items.
